meta.title: For better or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives
meta.deck: Every summer, a sleepy town in central Finland plays host to one of the world's oddest sporting events.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

pronounce.253.5: two hundred and fifty-three and a half

sents.en: For better or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives
sents.zh: 无论顺境还是逆境：芬兰男人背着妻子赛跑的比赛
notes: for better or for worse：婚礼誓词“无论好坏”，这里一语双关：既指婚姻，也暗示这项运动说不上好坏。
the race where ...：where 引导定语从句，修饰 race。

sents.en: Every summer, a sleepy town in central Finland plays host to one of the world's oddest sporting events.
sents.zh: 每年夏天，芬兰中部一个安静的小镇都会举办一项全世界最古怪的体育赛事。
notes: sleepy：（地方）冷清的、不热闹的。
play host to：举办、作东道主。
one of the + 最高级 + 复数名词：最……的……之一。

sents.en: The rules are simple, the prize is beer, and nobody takes it entirely seriously.
sents.zh: 规则很简单，奖品是啤酒，而且没有人完全把它当回事。
notes: 三个并列短句，节奏轻快。
take sth seriously：认真对待。not entirely：不完全。

sents.en: Sonkajärvi, a town of a few thousand people, is not an obvious place to stage a world championship.
sents.zh: 松卡耶尔维是个只有几千人的小镇，按理说不像是举办世界锦标赛的地方。
notes: a town of a few thousand people：同位语，补充说明小镇。
stage：举办、上演（活动、比赛）。
not an obvious place to ...：不是一个一看就适合……的地方。

sents.en: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.
sents.zh: 然而每年七月，成千上万的游客涌向这里，看男人们肩上扛着一个女人在泥地里飞奔。
notes: descend on：（大批人）突然涌向某地。
watch sb do：看某人做某事（全过程）。
with a woman slung over their shoulders：with + 宾语 + 过去分词，描述伴随状态。

sents.en: The sport, known in Finnish as eukonkanto, has been held there since 1992.
sents.zh: 这项运动芬兰语叫 eukonkanto（背妻），从 1992 年起就在这里举办。
notes: known in Finnish as ...：插入的过去分词短语，“在芬兰语里叫作……”。
has been held since ...：现在完成时被动，从过去一直持续到现在。

sents.en: Its origins, supposedly, lie in the 19th century.
sents.zh: 据说它的起源可以追溯到 19 世纪。
notes: origins：起源，常用复数。
supposedly：据说（说话人不一定相信）。
lie in：在于、存在于。

sents.en: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.
sents.zh: 当地民间传说讲到一个叫赫尔科·罗斯沃-龙凯宁的强盗，据说他会让想入伙的人背着沉重的麻袋穿过森林，以此考验他们。
notes: folklore：民间传说。tell of：讲述。
who is said to have tested ...：据说曾经考验过……（to have done 表示过去的事）。
would-be：想要成为……的、未来的。

sents.en: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.
sents.zh: 这个故事更阴暗的版本说，他的手下会袭击附近的村子，把女人抢走。
notes: tale：故事、传说。
have + 人 + doing：（故事里）描写某人在做……。
raid：突袭。run off with：带着……跑掉。

sents.en: Whether any of this happened is anyone's guess; the town is happy to cash in on the legend either way.
sents.zh: 这些事有没有发生过，谁也说不准；不管怎样，小镇都乐于借这个传说赚钱。
notes: Whether ... happened 作主语：……是否发生过。
anyone's guess：谁也说不准。
cash in on：利用……赚钱、捞好处。

sents.en: Historians may scoff, but a good story has never hurt tourism.
sents.zh: 历史学家也许会嗤之以鼻，但一个好故事从来不会对旅游业有坏处。
notes: scoff：嘲笑、嗤之以鼻。
may ..., but ...：让步，“也许……，但是……”。

sents.en: The course is 253.5 metres long and features two dry obstacles and a water pit about a metre deep.
sents.zh: 赛道长 253.5 米，有两个陆地障碍和一个大约一米深的水坑。
notes: feature 作动词：以……为特色、包含。
obstacle：障碍物。
a water pit about a metre deep：about a metre deep 后置修饰 pit。

sents.en: The "wife" does not have to be married to the carrier, or, indeed, to anyone.
sents.zh: 这位“妻子”不一定要和背她的人结婚，事实上，她跟谁结没结婚都无所谓。
notes: does not have to：不必。
or, indeed, ...：甚至、其实，用来补充一个更进一步的说法。

sents.en: She must, however, be over 17 and weigh at least 49kg; anyone lighter is weighed down with a rucksack of ballast to make up the difference.
sents.zh: 不过，她必须年满 17 岁，体重至少 49 公斤；不够重的人要背一个装着配重的背包，把差的重量补上。
notes: however 插在句中：不过。
weigh down：压住、使负重。
ballast：压舱物、配重。make up the difference：补足差额。

sents.en: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.
sents.zh: 大多数队伍选择所谓的“爱沙尼亚背法”：妻子头朝下倒挂，双腿勾住男人的脖子，双臂紧紧抱住他的腰。
notes: opt for：选择。so-called：所谓的。
in which ...：介词 + which 引导定语从句。
upside down：倒挂、颠倒。clasp：紧紧抱住、扣紧。

sents.en: It looks undignified, but it frees up the carrier's hands and keeps the weight close to his back.
sents.zh: 这姿势看起来很不体面，但它能空出背人者的双手，让重量紧贴他的后背。
notes: undignified：不体面的、有失尊严的。
free up：空出来、腾出来。

sents.en: Estonian couples were so good at it that they dominated the event for much of the 2000s.
sents.zh: 爱沙尼亚的情侣们太擅长这个了，在 2000 年代的大部分时间里都称霸这项赛事。
notes: so ... that ...：如此……以至于……。
dominate：主宰、称霸。

sents.en: The winners take home the wife's weight in beer, which makes a heavier partner a burden on the course but a bonus on the podium.
sents.zh: 冠军能带走和妻子体重一样重的啤酒，所以重一点的搭档在赛道上是负担，到了领奖台上却成了福利。
notes: the wife's weight in beer：和妻子体重等重的啤酒。
which 指前面整件事。
burden：负担。bonus：额外的好处。podium：领奖台。

sents.en: Many entrants turn up in fancy dress, cheer each other on and fall into the water pit with gusto.
sents.zh: 很多参赛者穿着奇装异服来，互相加油打气，还兴高采烈地摔进水坑里。
notes: entrant：参赛者。turn up：出现（已学）。in fancy dress：穿着化装服。
cheer sb on：为某人加油。
with gusto：兴致勃勃地。

sents.en: Spectators lap it up.
sents.zh: 观众们看得津津有味。
notes: lap sth up：（热切地）欣赏、享受；本义是动物舔着喝。
短句收尾，增加节奏感。

sents.en: Yet the top contenders train for months, because shaving a second off their time can mean the difference between glory and a long, wet walk home.
sents.zh: 然而顶尖的选手会训练好几个月，因为把成绩缩短一秒，就可能是荣耀和湿漉漉地走回家之间的差别。
notes: contender：有力的竞争者。
shave sth off：（一点点）削减。shaving ... 动名词作主语。
mean the difference between A and B：决定是 A 还是 B。

sents.en: The idea has spread: similar races are now held in America and Britain, among other places.
sents.zh: 这个点子已经传开了：美国、英国等地现在也会举办类似的比赛。
notes: 冒号后面具体说明前半句。
among other places：还有其他地方。

sents.en: Some purists complain that the spin-offs miss the point.
sents.zh: 一些较真的人抱怨说，这些衍生比赛没抓住重点。
notes: purist：纯粹主义者、坚持传统的人。
spin-off：衍生产品、派生出来的东西。
miss the point：没抓住要点。

sents.en: The point, the organisers insist, is not really about winning at all; it is about letting your hair down in a country often stereotyped as quiet and reserved.
sents.zh: 组织者坚持说，重点根本不在于输赢，而在于放松一下，尤其是在一个常被认为安静又内敛的国家。
notes: the organisers insist 是插入语。not ... at all：根本不。
let your hair down：放松、尽情玩乐。
be stereotyped as：被刻板地认为是……。reserved：内敛的、矜持的。

sents.en: And for the couples who make it to the finish, there is a lesson worth remembering: marriage, like the course, goes better when you pull together and keep your footing in the mud.
sents.zh: 对冲过终点的夫妻来说，还有一个值得记住的道理：婚姻就像这条赛道，同心协力、在泥泞中站稳脚跟，才会走得更顺。
notes: make it to：成功到达。worth remembering：值得记住。
pull together：齐心协力。
keep your footing：站稳脚跟。

vocab.note: 来自婚礼誓词 for better, for worse（无论顺境逆境）。日常也说“不管结果是好是坏”：For better or worse, the decision has been made.

ex.en: [[For better or worse]], we're stuck with this car.
ex.zh: 不管好坏，我们只能用这辆车了。

ex.en: They promised to stay together [[for better or for worse]].
ex.zh: 他们承诺无论顺境逆境都要在一起。

vocab.def: whatever happens, whether the result is good or bad

vocab.note: 本义“困的”；形容城镇、村子时是“冷清、没什么活动”：a sleepy village（安静的小村庄）。

ex.en: We spent a week in a [[sleepy]] fishing village.
ex.zh: 我们在一个安静的渔村住了一周。

ex.en: The baby is getting [[sleepy]].
ex.zh: 宝宝开始犯困了。

vocab.def: (of a place) quiet, with not much activity; tired and ready to sleep

vocab.note: 作动词：stage an event / a concert / a protest（举办活动、音乐会、抗议）。名词是“舞台；阶段”。

ex.en: The city will [[stage]] the next Olympic Games.
ex.zh: 这座城市将举办下一届奥运会。

ex.en: Workers [[staged]] a protest outside the factory.
ex.zh: 工人们在工厂外举行了抗议。

vocab.def: to organize an event, especially a public one; to perform a play

vocab.note: 很多人一下子来到某地：Fans descended on the stadium.（球迷涌向体育场。）也可以说亲戚“突然来访”。

ex.en: Thousands of tourists [[descend on]] the island every summer.
ex.zh: 每年夏天都有成千上万的游客涌上这座岛。

ex.en: My relatives [[descended on]] us for the holidays.
ex.zh: 假期亲戚们一窝蜂地来了我家。

vocab.def: (of a large number of people) to arrive at a place, often suddenly

vocab.note: 短距离全速跑：sprint for the bus（冲去赶公交）。名词 a sprint（短跑、冲刺）。

ex.en: I had to [[sprint]] to catch the last train.
ex.zh: 我得拼命跑才赶上末班车。

ex.en: She [[sprinted]] towards the finish line.
ex.zh: 她向终点线冲刺。

vocab.def: to run very fast for a short distance

cf.diff: jog 是为了锻炼慢慢地跑；sprint 是短距离用尽全力冲刺。

ex.en: I [[jog]] in the park every morning.
ex.zh: 我每天早上在公园慢跑。

vocab.note: 过去式、过去分词都是 slung。sling a bag over your shoulder（把包往肩上一甩）。名词 sling 是“吊带、三角巾”。

ex.en: He [[slung]] his jacket over the back of the chair.
ex.zh: 他把外套往椅背上一搭。

ex.en: She walked in with a bag [[slung over]] her shoulder.
ex.zh: 她肩上挎着个包走了进来。

vocab.def: to put something somewhere in a careless or quick way, often over your shoulder

vocab.note: 表示“起源”时常用复数：the origins of the festival。也指人的出身：of humble origins（出身卑微）。形容词 original。

ex.en: Nobody is sure about the [[origins]] of the song.
ex.zh: 没人确定这首歌的来历。

ex.en: The word has Latin [[origins]].
ex.zh: 这个词源自拉丁语。

vocab.def: the point or place where something begins; a person's family background

vocab.note: 表示“大家都这么说”，但说话人带点怀疑：The house is supposedly haunted.（据说这房子闹鬼。）

ex.en: The film is [[supposedly]] based on a true story.
ex.zh: 据说这部电影是根据真实故事改编的。

ex.en: He's [[supposedly]] the best cook in town.
ex.zh: 据说他是镇上最好的厨师。

vocab.def: according to what is generally believed or said, although it may not be true

cf.diff: be supposed to do 常表示“应该做（按规定或计划）”：You're supposed to wear a helmet.；supposedly 是副词“据说”，不能表示“应该”。

ex.en: You're [[supposed to]] be at work by nine.
ex.zh: 你应该九点前到公司。

vocab.note: 一个地方流传下来的故事、习俗和信仰，不可数：Irish folklore（爱尔兰民间传说）。

ex.en: In local [[folklore]], the lake is home to a monster.
ex.zh: 根据当地传说，这湖里住着一只怪物。

ex.en: She studies Scandinavian [[folklore]].
ex.zh: 她研究斯堪的纳维亚的民间传说。

vocab.def: the traditional stories and beliefs of a community, passed on by word of mouth

vocab.note: 放在名词前：would-be actors（想当演员的人）、a would-be thief（企图行窃的人）。

ex.en: The course is popular with [[would-be]] writers.
ex.zh: 这门课很受想当作家的人欢迎。

ex.en: A [[would-be]] thief was caught by the shop owner.
ex.zh: 一个企图行窃的人被店主抓住了。

vocab.def: wanting or trying to be a particular type of person

vocab.note: 多指虚构的、传说的或夸张的故事：fairy tale（童话）、tell tales（打小报告）。

ex.en: Grandma told us [[tales]] of ghosts and witches.
ex.zh: 奶奶给我们讲鬼和女巫的故事。

ex.en: It's a [[tale]] of love and loss.
ex.zh: 这是一个关于爱与失去的故事。

vocab.def: a story, especially one that is imaginary or hard to believe

cf.diff: tale 和 tail 读音完全一样 /teɪl/：tale 是故事，tail 是尾巴。

ex.en: The dog wagged its [[tail]].
ex.zh: 狗摇了摇尾巴。

vocab.zh: 突袭、袭击；（警察）突击搜查
vocab.note: 动词、名词同形：a police raid（警察突击搜查）。口语还可以说 raid the fridge（翻冰箱找吃的）。

ex.en: Police [[raided]] the building at dawn.
ex.zh: 警察在黎明时突袭了这栋楼。

ex.en: The kids [[raided]] the fridge after school.
ex.zh: 孩子们放学后把冰箱翻了个遍。

vocab.def: to attack a place suddenly; (of police) to enter a place suddenly to search it

cf.diff: invade 是军队大规模“入侵、占领”一个国家；raid 是短时间的“突袭”，打完就走。

ex.en: The army [[invaded]] the country.
ex.zh: 军队入侵了这个国家。

vocab.zh: （故事、说法里）描写某人在做……；让某人一直做……
vocab.note: have + 宾语 + doing：①（某个版本、故事）把某人写成在做……：The legend has him living in a cave.（传说中他住在山洞里。）②让某人持续做某事：He had us laughing all night.（他让我们笑了一整晚。）

ex.en: The old story [[has]] the king hiding in a tree.
ex.zh: 那个古老的故事里，国王躲在一棵树上。

ex.en: The comedian [[had]] us laughing all night.
ex.zh: 那位喜剧演员让我们笑了一整晚。

vocab.conn: 主语（故事、版本、人）+ have + 宾语 + doing
vocab.say: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages

pick.q: The film ___ the hero living alone on an island.
pick.why: “电影把主角描写成独自住在岛上”，用 have sb doing。make sb do 后接动词原形。

pick.q: Within minutes, the clown had the children ___.
pick.why: have sb doing：让某人一直在做……，用 -ing。

vocab.note: be anyone's guess：没人知道答案：What happens next is anyone's guess.（接下来会怎样谁也说不准。）

ex.en: Why he left is [[anyone's guess]].
ex.zh: 他为什么走，谁也说不准。

ex.en: When the train will arrive is [[anyone's guess]].
ex.zh: 火车什么时候到，谁也不知道。

vocab.def: something that nobody can know for certain

vocab.note: 趁机利用某个机会赚钱，常带点贬义：Shops cash in on the World Cup.（商店借世界杯赚钱。）

ex.en: Hotels [[cash in on]] the festival by raising prices.
ex.zh: 酒店借节日涨价赚钱。

ex.en: He was accused of [[cashing in on]] his famous name.
ex.zh: 他被指责利用自己的名气捞好处。

vocab.def: to make money or gain an advantage from a situation, often unfairly

vocab.note: scoff at sth：嘲笑、不屑：People scoffed at the idea.（人们对这个主意嗤之以鼻。）英式口语里还可指“狼吞虎咽”。

ex.en: They [[scoffed]] at my plan, but it worked.
ex.zh: 他们嘲笑我的计划，可它成功了。

ex.en: Don't [[scoff]]; it could happen.
ex.zh: 别不屑，这是有可能的。

vocab.def: to laugh at or talk about something in a way that shows you think it is stupid

cf.diff: 形近词：scoff 是“嘲笑、不屑”；scold 是“责骂（孩子等）”。

ex.en: His mum [[scolded]] him for being late.
ex.zh: 他妈妈骂他回来晚了。

vocab.zh: 以……为特色、包含；（电影等）由……主演
vocab.note: 作动词：The hotel features a rooftop pool.（酒店的特色是有个屋顶泳池。）名词是“特点、特征”。

ex.en: The new phone [[features]] a larger screen.
ex.zh: 新手机配备了更大的屏幕。

ex.en: The film [[features]] several famous actors.
ex.zh: 这部电影有好几位明星出演。

vocab.def: to include something as an important part

vocab.note: 可以是真实的障碍物（obstacle course 障碍赛道），也可以是抽象的困难：an obstacle to success（成功路上的障碍）。

ex.en: Money is the biggest [[obstacle]] to our plans.
ex.zh: 钱是我们计划最大的障碍。

ex.en: The horse jumped over every [[obstacle]].
ex.zh: 那匹马跳过了每一个障碍。

vocab.def: something that blocks your way or makes it difficult to do something

vocab.note: or, indeed, ...：用来补充一个更进一步的说法，“甚至……”。也可加强语气：Thank you very much indeed.（真的非常感谢。）

ex.en: Few people, [[indeed]] almost nobody, came.
ex.zh: 来的人很少，其实几乎没人来。

ex.en: It was a very good meal [[indeed]].
ex.zh: 这顿饭真的很好吃。

vocab.def: used to add a stronger point; used to emphasize that something is true

vocab.note: be weighed down with/by：被……压着（字面或比喻）：weighed down with shopping（提着一大堆购物袋）、weighed down by worries（忧心忡忡）。

ex.en: She was [[weighed down]] with heavy bags.
ex.zh: 她拎着沉重的袋子。

ex.en: He felt [[weighed down]] by his debts.
ex.zh: 他被债务压得喘不过气。

vocab.def: to make someone or something heavy; to make someone feel worried

vocab.note: 船、热气球等为了平稳而装的重物；这里指为了达到体重要求而背的重物。不可数。

ex.en: The ship carried rocks as [[ballast]].
ex.zh: 这艘船装着石头当压舱物。

ex.en: The balloon rose when they dropped the [[ballast]].
ex.zh: 他们扔掉配重后，气球升了起来。

vocab.def: heavy material carried to make something more stable or to add weight

vocab.note: 比 choose 正式：opt for sth / opt to do sth。opt out（选择不参加）。名词 option（选项）。

ex.en: Most people [[opt for]] the cheaper ticket.
ex.zh: 大多数人会选便宜的票。

ex.en: We [[opted for]] a quiet wedding.
ex.zh: 我们选择了一场简单的婚礼。

vocab.def: to choose one thing instead of others

cf.diff: choose 最普通；opt for 稍正式，强调“在几个选项中经过考虑选了某一个”。

ex.en: [[Choose]] a card, any card.
ex.zh: 选一张牌，随便哪张。

vocab.note: 上下颠倒：hang upside down（倒挂）。比喻“弄得乱七八糟”：turn the house upside down（把家翻得乱七八糟）。

ex.en: The picture is hanging [[upside down]].
ex.zh: 这幅画挂倒了。

ex.en: We turned the house [[upside down]] looking for the keys.
ex.zh: 我们为了找钥匙把家里翻了个底朝天。

vocab.def: with the top part at the bottom; in a very untidy state

cf.diff: upside down 是上下颠倒；inside out 是里外翻过来（衣服穿反了）。

ex.en: You're wearing your jumper [[inside out]].
ex.zh: 你的毛衣穿反了。

vocab.note: 用手或手臂紧紧握住、抱住：clasp your hands（双手紧握）。名词是“搭扣、扣子”。

ex.en: She [[clasped]] the letter to her chest.
ex.zh: 她把信紧紧贴在胸前。

ex.en: He sat with his hands [[clasped]] in his lap.
ex.zh: 他双手交握放在腿上坐着。

vocab.def: to hold something or someone tightly with your hands or arms

cf.diff: grasp 是“一把抓住”，还可以表示“理解”；clasp 强调“紧紧抱住、握住不放”，常带情感。

ex.en: She [[grasped]] the rope with both hands.
ex.zh: 她双手抓住了绳子。

vocab.note: dignified（庄重的、有尊严的）加 un-。常用来形容姿势、行为难看、丢脸。

ex.en: Falling off the stage was rather [[undignified]].
ex.zh: 从舞台上摔下来实在有点丢脸。

ex.en: He thought dancing in public was [[undignified]].
ex.zh: 他觉得在公共场合跳舞有失体面。

vocab.def: making you look silly or lose the respect of others

cf.diff: dignified 是“庄重、有尊严的”，undignified 正好相反。

ex.en: She remained calm and [[dignified]].
ex.zh: 她始终保持冷静庄重。

vocab.note: 把时间、空间、资金等腾出来：free up some space（腾出些空间）、free up your hands（空出双手）。

ex.en: Deleting old photos will [[free up]] space on your phone.
ex.zh: 删掉旧照片能腾出手机空间。

ex.en: The new system [[frees up]] staff for other work.
ex.zh: 新系统让员工能腾出手做别的工作。

vocab.def: to make something available for use

vocab.note: dominate a sport / a market（称霸某项运动/市场）。名词 dominance，形容词 dominant。

ex.en: Two companies [[dominate]] the market.
ex.zh: 两家公司主宰着这个市场。

ex.en: The news was [[dominated]] by the election.
ex.zh: 新闻全被选举占据了。

vocab.def: to be the most powerful or successful; to control

vocab.note: 可以是真的重物，也可以是责任、压力：a financial burden（经济负担）、be a burden on sb（成为某人的负担）。

ex.en: I don't want to be a [[burden]] on my children.
ex.zh: 我不想成为孩子们的负担。

ex.en: The new tax is a heavy [[burden]] for small shops.
ex.zh: 新税对小店来说是沉重的负担。

vocab.def: something heavy that you have to carry; a difficult responsibility

vocab.note: 原意是“奖金”（a Christmas bonus）；也指意外的好处：The view is a bonus.（风景是额外的福利。）

ex.en: All staff got a [[bonus]] at Christmas.
ex.zh: 所有员工圣诞节都拿到了奖金。

ex.en: The hotel was cheap, and the sea view was a [[bonus]].
ex.zh: 酒店很便宜，海景还是额外福利。

vocab.def: an extra amount of money; something good that you get in addition to what you expected

vocab.note: 比赛前三名站的台子：stand on the podium（登上领奖台）。也指演讲者站的台。

ex.en: She finished third and stepped onto the [[podium]].
ex.zh: 她获得第三名，登上了领奖台。

ex.en: The speaker walked up to the [[podium]].
ex.zh: 演讲者走上讲台。

vocab.def: a small raised platform where winners stand or a speaker stands

vocab.note: 参加比赛、考试的人：All entrants must be over 18.。动词 enter（报名参加）。

ex.en: Every [[entrant]] receives a free T-shirt.
ex.zh: 每位参赛者都会得到一件免费T恤。

ex.en: There were over 500 [[entrants]] this year.
ex.zh: 今年有 500 多名参赛者。

vocab.def: a person who takes part in a competition or exam

cf.diff: 形近词：entrant 是参赛的人；entrance 是“入口、进入”。

ex.en: Meet me at the main [[entrance]].
ex.zh: 在正门口等我。

vocab.note: cheer sb on：大声为某人加油鼓劲。cheer up 是“使高兴起来”。

ex.en: The crowd [[cheered on]] the runners.
ex.zh: 观众为跑步的人加油。

ex.en: Come and [[cheer them on]] on Saturday!
ex.zh: 周六来为他们加油吧！

vocab.def: to shout encouragement to someone who is competing

cf.diff: cheer sb on 是为比赛的人加油；cheer sb up 是让难过的人开心起来。

ex.en: This song always [[cheers]] me [[up]].
ex.zh: 这首歌总能让我开心起来。

vocab.zh: 兴致勃勃地、津津有味地
vocab.note: gusto 是“热情、兴致”，几乎只用在 with gusto 里：sing with gusto（放声高歌）、eat with gusto（吃得很香）。

ex.en: The children sang [[with gusto]].
ex.zh: 孩子们兴高采烈地唱着歌。

ex.en: He ate his dinner [[with gusto]].
ex.zh: 他吃晚饭吃得津津有味。

vocab.def: with great enthusiasm and enjoyment

vocab.note: 本义是动物用舌头舔着喝；比喻热烈地享受、照单全收（赞美、关注等）：The audience lapped it up.

ex.en: The cat [[lapped up]] the milk.
ex.zh: 猫把牛奶舔光了。

ex.en: She told silly jokes and the kids [[lapped it up]].
ex.zh: 她讲了些傻笑话，孩子们听得乐不可支。

vocab.def: to enjoy something very much; to accept something eagerly

vocab.note: 有希望赢的参赛者：a strong contender for the title（冠军的有力争夺者）。动词 contend（竞争）。

ex.en: She is a serious [[contender]] for the gold medal.
ex.zh: 她是金牌的有力争夺者。

ex.en: Only three [[contenders]] are left in the race.
ex.zh: 比赛只剩下三名竞争者。

vocab.def: a person or team with a good chance of winning a competition

vocab.note: shave sth off sth：从……削减一点：shave two seconds off the record（把纪录缩短两秒）。本义是“刮（胡子）”。

ex.en: The new road [[shaves]] ten minutes off the journey.
ex.zh: 新路让行程缩短了十分钟。

ex.en: He [[shaved]] his beard off for the summer.
ex.zh: 夏天来了，他把胡子刮了。

vocab.def: to reduce something by a small amount

vocab.zh: 纯粹主义者、坚持传统的人
vocab.note: 坚持某事必须按传统、正宗方式做的人：Coffee purists drink it black.（咖啡纯粹主义者只喝黑咖啡。）

ex.en: Pizza [[purists]] say pineapple doesn't belong on it.
ex.zh: 披萨纯粹主义者说菠萝不该放上去。

ex.en: Some music [[purists]] hate the new version.
ex.zh: 一些音乐纯粹主义者讨厌新版本。

vocab.def: a person who believes things should be done in a traditional or correct way

vocab.note: 从原有事物衍生出来的东西：a TV spin-off（电视剧的衍生剧）。动词短语 spin off（衍生出、分拆）。

ex.en: The show was so popular that it got a [[spin-off]].
ex.zh: 这部剧太火了，还出了衍生剧。

ex.en: The toy is a [[spin-off]] from the film.
ex.zh: 这个玩具是电影的周边产品。

vocab.def: something new that develops from something that already exists

vocab.note: 完全没理解别人真正的意思：You're missing the point.（你没明白我的意思。）

ex.en: You're [[missing the point]]; it's not about money.
ex.zh: 你没抓住重点，这跟钱无关。

ex.en: Critics who called it silly [[missed the point]].
ex.zh: 说它很傻的评论家没明白它的意思。

vocab.def: to not understand the most important part of something

vocab.note: 放下平时的拘谨，好好放松一下：It's a party, let your hair down!（这是派对，放开玩吧！）

ex.en: After exams, students like to [[let their hair down]].
ex.zh: 考完试，学生们都喜欢放松一下。

ex.en: Come on, [[let your hair down]] for once!
ex.zh: 来吧，就放松这一次！

vocab.def: to relax and enjoy yourself, especially after being serious

vocab.zh: 对……有刻板印象；刻板印象
vocab.note: be stereotyped as：被刻板地认为是……。名词：a stereotype（刻板印象）。

ex.en: Scientists are often [[stereotyped]] as shy.
ex.zh: 科学家常被刻板地认为很害羞。

ex.en: Not every Briton fits the [[stereotype]].
ex.zh: 不是每个英国人都符合那种刻板印象。

vocab.def: to have a fixed and too simple idea about what a type of person or thing is like

vocab.note: 形容人：不太表露感情、话少。也有“预订的”意思：This seat is reserved.（这个座位有人订了。）

ex.en: He's quite [[reserved]] until you get to know him.
ex.zh: 在你熟悉他之前，他挺内敛的。

ex.en: Sorry, this table is [[reserved]].
ex.zh: 抱歉，这张桌子已经被预订了。

vocab.def: not showing your feelings or talking much about yourself

cf.diff: reserved 是内敛、不爱表露；outgoing 是外向、爱交朋友。

ex.en: She's very [[outgoing]] and makes friends easily.
ex.zh: 她很外向，很容易交到朋友。

vocab.note: 大家一起努力：We need to pull together.（我们得齐心协力。）pull yourself together 是“振作起来”。

ex.en: If we all [[pull together]], we can finish by Friday.
ex.zh: 只要我们齐心协力，周五就能完成。

ex.en: The town [[pulled together]] after the flood.
ex.zh: 洪水过后，全镇齐心协力。

vocab.def: to work together as a group to achieve something

vocab.note: 在滑的地方站稳不摔倒；比喻在困难中保持稳定。反义：lose one's footing（失足、站不稳）。

ex.en: It was hard to [[keep your footing]] on the icy path.
ex.zh: 在结冰的路上很难站稳。

ex.en: She [[lost her footing]] and fell into the river.
ex.zh: 她脚下一滑，掉进了河里。

vocab.def: to stay standing and not fall, especially on a slippery surface

cloze.hint: 无论好坏（for ___ or for worse）
挂在肩上（sling 的过去分词）
描写某人在做……（___ his men raiding）
被刻板地认为（过去分词）

breakdown.en: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.
points: 主干：Local folklore tells of a robber —— 当地传说讲到一个强盗。
called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen：过去分词短语，“名叫……的”。
who is said to have tested ...：非限制性定语从句；be said to have done = 据说曾经……。
by making them carry heavy sacks：by + doing 表示方式；make sb do（使役，后接动词原形）。
